cards.design_implication: If data centralization is challenging or infeasible to scale, a design may consider using federated learning to share model updates as a mechanism for collaboration.
does_not_establish: Specific mathematical formulas for model updates
Concrete hardware or software infrastructure requirements
cards.evidence_excerpt: Federated ML (FL) provides an alternative paradigm for accurate and generalizable ML, by only sharing numerical model updates.
limitations: The abstract defines the mechanism generally but does not detail specific technical implementations, communication protocols, or privacy guarantees.
cards.statement: Federated ML provides an alternative paradigm for accurate and generalizable ML by sharing numerical model updates instead of centralizing multi-site data.

cards.design_implication: Designs involving multi-site collaborations for rare diseases may reference this scale (71 sites, 6 continents) as a potential boundary condition for scalability.
cards.evidence_excerpt: involving data from 71 sites across 6 continents, to generate an automatic tumor boundary detector for the rare disease of glioblastoma
limitations: The abstract states the number of sites and continents but does not provide data regarding site selection criteria, geographic distribution details, or specific disease prevalence at each site.
cards.statement: The federated learning study was applied to data from 71 sites across 6 continents for glioblastoma tumor boundary detection.

cards.design_implication: Experimental designs for federated learning in this context could include comparison against publicly trained models as a baseline control.
does_not_establish: Definitions of the control group beyond it being a public model
Implementation details of the comparison protocol
limitations: The abstract identifies the existence of a comparison but does not define the specific architecture, training data, or hyperparameters of the publicly trained model.
cards.statement: The federated learning approach demonstrated improvement over a publicly trained model for tumor delineation.
